descriptionChirho: To actively gather or collect people, crops, or things together, the core Qal transitive sense of asap confirmed by Arabic jamaʿa and Korean 모았다/모으다.
To gather oneself or assemble as a group in reflexive/middle voice, confirmed by Arabic ijtamaʿa (Form VIII reflexive) and Swahili kukusanyika (reflexive -ika form).
Passive Nifal euphemism for death meaning to be gathered or joined to one's ancestors, confirmed by Arabic inḍamma (to join/be annexed) and Korean 모이리라 in funerary contexts.
Piel participial military sense meaning the one who gathers the rear, i.e. the rear guard of a marching column, confirmed by Arabic sāqa and Swahili walinzi wa nyuma.
Passive intensive sense of being gathered or assembled, the Pual forms, confirmed by Arabic yujmaʿu (passive) and Korean 거두어진다.
Extended Qal/Nifal sense of removing, taking away, or withdrawing something such as divine protection or wrath, confirmed by Arabic nazaʿa/azala/rafaʿa (remove) and Swahili ameondoa/imeondolewa.
Hifil causative sense of sweeping away or utterly consuming, an intensified removal often in prophetic judgment contexts, confirmed by Zephaniah context and Korean 끝내리라 (to bring to an end).
Disputed sense where asap appears to mean heal or restore, confirmed by Arabic yashfi (to heal) and Swahili kumponya/ataponya (to heal), likely a homographic root distinct from the gathering root.
